So 'User@Example.com' vs 'user@example.com' would slip through and create a duplicate attendee plus a duplicate invitation email. The frontend zod schema also does not enforce case-insensitive uniqueness. This is a real correctness defect verifiable from the diff.

judged_text: Existing-attendee deduplication is case-sensitive, allowing email case variants to create duplicate attendees and invitations

record.issue_text: Existing-attendee deduplication is case-sensitive, allowing email case variants to create duplicate attendees and invitations

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. In addGuests.handler.ts, the uniqueGuests filter uses direct string comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. This comparison is case-sensitive, meaning 'User@Example.com' would not match 'user@example.com' in the existing attendees list. This could allow duplicate attendees with different email case variants to be added, causing duplicate invitations. Email addresses should be compared case-insensitively (at least for the local part in practice, and definitely for the domain part per RFC 5321).
